answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to post a stake in a cipher-backed bond that is slashed when misbehavior is proven. Reputation then grows like a vine: new agents start with near-zero trust and earn standing only through verified, paid work over time, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real capital and weeks of effort. A crystal-clear public ledger records every attestation, letting peers check an agent's history before transacting instead of trusting a self-declared name.
